recentItems.title: Russian expert expects China to advance cooperation as BRICS 2027 chair
recentItems.description:
Ekaterina Zaklyazminskaya, head of the Center for World Politics and Strategic Analysis at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of China and Modern Asia, said that all sides are looking forward to China taking over the rotating presidency of BRICS next year.

She pointed out that BRICS countries are committed to promoting more practical cooperation, and she expects China to provide tangible support to countries around the world.

recentItems.title: Exclusive with former Jordanian Prime Minister Omar Razzaz
recentItems.description:
What can a country's cities reveal about its development, culture and governance? And what can China's experience offer the wider world? On Leaders Talk, CMG's He Yanke speaks with former Jordanian Prime Minister Omar Razzaz. Having visited China many times, Razzaz shares his observations on the country's modernization and explains why he believes China's cities offer a distinctive combination of modernity and cultural heritage. They explore China's 12345 citizen service hotline and examine how data-driven governance can improve public services and decision-making.

recentItems.title: How Gen Z sees the world: What makes Chinese innovation so cool? A Vietnamese vlogger at CIFTIS
recentItems.description:
The 2026 #China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing, has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, showcasing the latest technologies, products and innovations in the services sector.

In this episode of How Gen Z sees the world, Vietnamese vlogger Tiểu Thanh explores #CIFTIS firsthand. She puts on VR and MR headsets to examine cells in 360 degrees, tries an intelligent traditional Chinese medicine therapy bed, and steps into an AI-powered mobile medical vehicle to see how technology is transforming healthcare.

This year, CIFTIS also introduced an exhibition area for services helping Chinese companies expand overseas. Tiểu Thanh spoke with exhibitors about support for entering Southeast Asian markets, from overseas factory setup and cost estimates to local certifications.

From cutting-edge technology to cross-border services, Tiểu Thanh discovers that Chinese innovation is not just about technology, but also about helping Chinese companies connect with global markets.

recentItems.title: Beyond the Dollar: How Far Can BRICS Go?
recentItems.description:
Against the backdrop of conflict in Iran, rising energy prices and trade tensions, BRICS leaders are gathering in New Delhi for their annual summit.

One of the key issues on the table is how to make payments and trade between BRICS countries easier, including greater use of national currencies and closer links between their payment systems.

But how far can that cooperation really go? And what could it mean for the global economy, and for the future role of the US dollar?

On this edition of The Agenda, Juliet Mann is joined by Paulo Nogueira Batista Jr., founding vice president of the New Development Bank; Sanusha Naidu, senior research fellow at the Institute for Global Dialogue; former BRICS Sherpa Professor Sanjay Bhattacharyya; and Professor Shen Yi, director of the Center for BRICS Studies at Fudan University. #BRICS #economy #trade #payment

recentItems.title: Why Georgia is increasingly popular among Chinese tourists
recentItems.description:
Tourism constitutes about 8% of Georgia's economy and is a key part of trade in services. Irakli Nadareishvili, deputy minister of economy and sustainable development of Georgia, attended the ongoing China International Fair for Trade in Services in Beijing. He said Chinese visitors to Georgia grew nearly 50% last year, boosted by visa-free travel and direct flights, terming Georgia as a four-season destination. 

As trade in services opens new opportunities for both countries, he also invited Georgians to travel to China to experience the culture, history and cuisine.

recentItems.title: Indian scholar calls for closer China-India cooperation
recentItems.description:
【GUEST】

B. R. DEEPAK

Professor of Chinese and China Studies

Jawaharlal Nehru University, India

In an interview with CGTN, Professor B. R. Deepak of Jawaharlal Nehru University highlights BRICS' growing relevance and China's important role in its future. He also calls for the resumption of the China-India Strategic Economic Dialogue to advance bilateral cooperation.

The larger sections of the intelligentsia in this country, including many people in this university – they believe that BRICS remains one of the fundamental, foundational platforms for cooperation.

And the relevance is growing day by day. So we can see how BRICS, from just five countries in the past, has expanded into 11 and then plus 10 partner countries. So, therefore, the expanding nature of BRICS and especially, you can say, its population composition or its share in global trade, and also the global economic output – which should be around 40%.

And moreover, some of the practical measures on BRICS which are going on. For example, the grants and loans from the BRICS New Development Bank, which India has got to the tune of almost 9 billion US dollars and above for almost 13 projects which are going on, whether they are infrastructure-related, whether they are sanitation-related, whether they are clean energy-related.

We have many problems in the Global South. We have illiteracy; we have poverty – almost 700 million people in the Global South are still poor. So how do we elevate them from poverty? So what kind of model are you going to adopt, whether it is the American model or the Western model for modernization? Or is it the model for large populations to be modernized, and who has the experience for that? And naturally, another Global South country is China. Therefore, they are very clear that if you have to cooperate, you have to develop; you have to realize your industrialization and modernization; you need to bring China on board. Because China is there; whether you are willing or not willing to accept China as a pole or the strongest pole in BRICS, it is there. And you got to cooperate with China.

Many of the Indian people don't think big about China, right? Which is a flawed perspective. We have to recognize this fact that China is a big trading power. It's a big manufacturing hub. It has big technological prowess and it has made headway in the new technologies, which we really can benefit from.
